tools.summary: sdk-corpus-lay4490 — Zendesk — Change a ticket's status, priority, subject, assignee, tags or custom fields. On a ticket a customer is waiting on, they may answer: their reply comes back beside this call's body, under dynamics (each spoken turn's text), and is on the ticket as a new comment from the next read

assignee_id.description: An agent this desk holds, or null to unassign

custom_fields.description: Any of ['refund_amount', 'refund_card_last4', 'resolution_code']. refund_amount is whole cents; resolution_code is one of ['refunded', 'replaced', 'declined', 'duplicate']

tags.description: The ticket's tags, replacing the ones it carries

tools.summary: sdk-corpus-lay4490 — Zendesk — Reply to a ticket by adding a comment, public or internal. On a ticket a customer is waiting on, they may answer: their reply comes back beside this call's body, under dynamics (each spoken turn's text), and is on the ticket as a new comment from the next read

author_id.description: The agent the comment is by; the desk's first agent when omitted

examples: Thanks for the detail -- could you send a photo of the damage so I can process this?

public.description: True for a reply the requester can see, false for an internal note only agents read. Public when omitted, which is what a reply means

tools.name: zendesk__ZENDESK_SEARCH_ZENDESK
tools.summary: sdk-corpus-lay4490 — Zendesk — Search this desk's tickets, users and organizations with Zendesk's query syntax. Results are complete; there is no next page. Help-centre articles are listed by ZENDESK_LIST_HELP_CENTER_ARTICLES, not here

query.description: A Zendesk search. Operators this twin serves: type:, status:, priority:, tags:, requester:, assignee:, organization:, group:, created>, created<, updated>, updated<. Bare words match the subject and the description; '-' negates and a "quoted phrase" matches as one. Date operators resolve against this world's own today, never a wall clock

platform_tools.name: run_tasks
platform_tools.summary: This environment's task sets and tasks, by id, name and set, to choose what to run.

platform_tools.name: run_open
platform_tools.summary: Open a graded run of this environment's tasks: a set_name, task_ids, or neither for every task, at most 300. Needs an Automation key, as every run_* tool does. Returns the run_id and, per task, its task_id, prompt and call_url. Your agent calls the task's tools on its call_url (or sends run_id and task_id beside tool and args) with an Standard key; then submit its answer with run_answer.

platform_tools.name: run_answer
platform_tools.summary: Submit the final answer to one task of the run. Each task takes one answer.

platform_tools.name: run_get
platform_tools.summary: The run, and each task's verdict once the run is finished.

platform_tools.name: run_finish
platform_tools.summary: Finish the run with tasks still unanswered.
